doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Television, vocal albums and orchestral craft
title: The Mel Tormé album with Ellington and Basie tunes
summary: Mandel recalls the Tormé record on Duke and the Count, a collaboration that Mel called his favorite, with Mel giving a free hand.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: And around the same time you did the Mel Tormé record, I Like Duke, I Like the Count. [I Dig the Duke! I Dig the Count!]
That was a nice experience too. I honestly think that – Mel told me it’s his favorite record.
Yeah, he really likes that, one of the best he ever did.
Yeah, I think probably that one and the two with Marty Paich with the Dek-Tette.
Yeah, those are probably his finest, from my admittedly subjective opinion.
Now somebody like Mel, is someone who taught himself to orchestrate and…
Does he get more involved with an arranger in terms of dictating what he wants or does he give you a freehand or how does he operate?

He gave me a freehand, but he gave me some input here and there and I gave him a lot of input. I don’t know, it was a very nice collaboration, it was effortless. We both agreed on what we wanted to do, if he had an idea here I’d write it down very quickly and do it.
And as far as the material it was probably a labor of love just because you were both Ellington and Basie fans…
It was just a matter of what did he want to sing.
